concepts.def: Feeling pushed by someone in charge
Rules about doing the right thing

walkthroughs.body_html:
Obedience is doing what someone with authority tells you to.

It's different from conformity — conformity is the group, obedience is the leader.

In 1963 Stanley Milgram told participants to give 'shocks' to a 'learner' (an actor) for wrong answers.

The shocks weren't real — but participants didn't know.

Shockingly, 65% went to the highest level when a man in a white coat told them to. 😬

It taught us:

  • Ordinary people can do harmful things under orders.
  • Authority matters more than personality.
  • Speak up when something feels wrong.

Today's ethics rules stop such studies from happening unsafely. 📜

options: Just grabbing whoever is around (any haphazard method).
Every member of the target population has an equal chance of selection.
Picking participants who match the population profile.
